objective: CONTRA-READ-20261108-001's selected next step, approved by the coordinator under the owner's standing mandate (2026-11-08): prove that one row of creation between glue lines reads whether the removed line's three points are tied in the glue without it, or locate the gap. Test the statement beyond the trisum glues, on random cubic glues with a class without solutions, and reduce it to lemmas about the K4^(3) far side at lines meeting the removed line once and about degenerate gluings. No time constraints.
status: Complete 2026-11-08: partially successful. The proof attempt found the statement false in general: on 19 random cubic glues of 8 to 10 lines with a class without solutions, one row of creation fails to read the removed line's tie exactly at the 16 lines lying in a two-vertex cut of the incidence graph (sides of one more point than lines, one of them K4^(3) without a line), and reads it on every 3-connected glue tested (11 random, 7 trisum). K4^(3)'s silence under the tie, the apparent mechanism, fails on a 12-line trisum glue; no single near point makes K4^(3) create (proved, exhaustive). Refined conjecture: one row reads the tie on 3-connected glues. Next: why two-vertex cuts hide the tie (2/3)
stop_rule: Stop when the statement is proved for a stated family of glues, or a counterexample bounds it, or a precise gap is stated with the computed evidence on each side.
title: Why one row of creation reads the removed line's tie
